claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children. Let me start with a few questions.

**First, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm inquiring about my one child, Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about one child, Alex.

To assess eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to gather some details about your circumstances.

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 8 years old - he was born in 2016.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. So Alex was born in 2016 and is currently 8 years old.

**Are you the parent or guardian with primary responsibility for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's the thing - Alex doesn't actually live with me. He lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see, thank you for clarifying that. That's important information.

**Are you still involved in supporting Alex financially, even though he doesn't live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently contributing financially towards Alex's upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that you live in the UK.

Just to clarify further - **are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK? Or are you a national of an EEA country or Switzerland?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Is Alex a British citizen, or does he have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is a British citizen as well.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have the key information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've shared:
- Alex is 8 years old (born in 2016)
- Alex does not live with you
- You are not currently contributing financially towards Alex's upkeep
- You are a British citizen
- Alex is a British citizen

Unfortunately, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. One of the key eligibility requirements is that the child must **live with you**. Since Alex lives with his mother and you are not the person with primary responsibility for him or contributing to his financial support, you cannot claim Child Benefit for him.

The person with primary responsibility for Alex (likely his mother) would be the one able to claim Child Benefit on his behalf, provided they meet the other eligibility criteria.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. That makes sense. So because Alex lives with his mum and she's the one looking after him day-to-day, she would be the one who could claim it, not me?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Exactly, that's correct! Since Alex lives with his mother and she has primary responsibility for his day-to-day care, she would be the person eligible to claim Child Benefit for him, provided she also meets the other eligibility requirements (such as being a British citizen or having settled status, and living in the UK).

Child Benefit is designed to support the person who is responsible for looking after the child, and that's typically the person the child lives with.

Let me now provide you with my formal assessment:
